body:
Spin-off from #2088

Current requirement:

| # | Description | L1 | L2 | L3 | CWE |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **14.2.1** | Verify that all components are up to date, preferably using a dependency checker during build or compile time. | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | 1026 |

Some comments to keep ind mind:

* https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2088#issuecomment-2355412099
* https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2088#issuecomment-2362818721
* https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2088#issuecomment-2362912214


My proposal:

| # | Description | L1 | L2 | L3 | CWE |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **14.2.1** | Verify that all components are up to date. Note that updating only to patch publically known vulnerabilities relies on confidence that the vendor does not fix security holes without public announcements. | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | 1026 |

The "Note" part can be also part of the chapter text.

comments.body: There are significant unpublished security vulnerabilities. I hate to suggest it because it’s hard work, but I’d rather see folks er on the side of patching even if the SCA scanners say it’s clear. Especially server side. Less so client side.
What is the point in your comment, what it suggests what is not suggested?
I do not think we should suggest _not patching unless its a known published vuln_ for L3. I think this requirement should be removed.
What exact part of my proposal says that?

This sentence implies it. And "publically" is spelled wrong (should be "publicly")

_Note that updating only to patch publically known vulnerabilities relies on confidence that the vendor does not fix security holes without public announcements._

If that is not what you meant I suggest clarifying it.
The requirement says that you need to be up to date. The note points out, that if you update only for patched for **publicly** known issues, it contains security risk.

Let me suggest clarifying it so its more obvious.

_Note that while being up-to-date with patches is essential, relying solely on updates for publicly disclosed vulnerabilities introduces risk, as vendors may fix security issues without public announcements._
With this wording I prefer it to be part of the section text.
I think that is very reasonable!
Re-open fpr moving it to V10.6
